title: Pulmonary fibrosis, scleroderma lung, tracheostomy and ventilator
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's lung fibrosis or airway status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for tracheostomy and ventilator management.

HPI
Pt is an 83y female seen for routine follow-up of tracheostomy and home ventilator use. Pt has been dependent on the ventilator at night and during parts of the day following a past illness. She reports stable status and no acute distress today. Trach care was reviewed with pt and caregiver. Pt denies any recent infections or equipment malfunctions.

Medication List
1. Levofloxacin 500mg QD
2. Pantoprazole 40mg QD
3. Guaifenesin 600mg PRN

Exam
Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, RR 18, SpO2 95% on ventilator.
Gen: Alert, well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: Tracheostomy site clean, no signs of infection or irritation. Breath sounds clear.
Neuro: Oriented x3.

Assessment
1. Tracheostomy status.
2. Home ventilator dependence.

Plan
- Continue current ventilator settings as prescribed.
- Continue trach care as reviewed today.
- F/u in 3 months or PRN.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Tracheostomy status, Z93.0, plus dependence on a ventilator, Z99.11 (both HCC 211).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J84, M34, Z93, Z99

distractors.why: Ventilator dependence is documented: add Z99.11.
